opening.text: Some mornings begin gray and cold. Then the sun clears the hills, and everything changes. The frost melts. People step outside. Nobody asked the sun for anything. It just shone. A kind word or a kind act can do that for a person. It doesn't fix everything. But it warms the day.

mainMessage.text: Kindness is like morning sun. It warms the people near us without asking for anything.

blocks.text: **Heaven's way of living** Kindness isn't a small virtue. It belongs to the life God wants for us.
Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering;
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is the essence of a celestial life.
Kindness belongs in heaven's life.
**How Christ treats people** We can tell a lot about a person by how they treat others. The Savior is our pattern.
And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is how a Christlike person treats others.
Treat people as He does.
**It opens doors** Kindness makes room for friendship. It does what money can't.
Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is a passport that opens doors and fashions friends.
Kindness opens doors.
**Everyone is a neighbor** The sun doesn't pick who gets light. Our kindness shouldn't pick either.
Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves? And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.
Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Remember This: Kindness Begins with Me” from the April 2011 general conference.
Jesus taught us through this story that everyone is our neighbor.
Shine on everyone.
**Warmth that lingers** Sunlight stays in a stone long after the sun is gone. Kind words stay in us too.
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kind words not only lift our spirits in the moment they are given, but they can linger with us over the years.
Kind words last.
**Like our Father** Heavenly Father is kind to us. We learn it from Him.

And charity suffereth long, and is kind, and envieth not, and is not puffed up, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil, and rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in the truth, beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
As Heavenly Father is kind, we also should be kind to others.
Be kind as He is kind.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone's kindness changed their day. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Boaz and Ruth

blocks.text: Ruth was a stranger in a new land. She worked in a field to feed her mother-in-law. Boaz noticed.

Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said unto him, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? Then she said, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord; for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken friendly unto thine handmaid, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens.
Boaz spoke to her kindly. He made her feel safe. Ruth never forgot it. Neither will a person you treat gently.

opening.text: Ever heard a door hinge squeak? One drop of oil, and the noise is gone. The door swings easily. Nothing was broken. It just needed a little smoothing. Many hard moments between people are like that. A gentle word is the oil.

mainMessage.text: Kindness is the drop of oil that keeps life between people from squeaking and sticking.

Kindness is the essence of a celestial life.
Kindness is heaven's oil.

Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is how a Christlike person treats others.
Be gentle like Him.
**A smoother way in** Where there is friction, kindness helps. It opens the door and makes friends.
Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is a passport that opens doors and fashions friends.
Smooth the way.
**Every door** We don't oil only the doors we like. The Savior taught that everyone is our neighbor.
Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves? And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.
Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Remember This: Kindness Begins with Me” from the April 2011 general conference.
Jesus taught us through this story that everyone is our neighbor.
Every door counts.
**The oil soaks in** Oil stays on the hinge for months. A kind word can stay with a person for years.
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kind words not only lift our spirits in the moment they are given, but they can linger with us over the years.
A soft answer lasts.
**Learned from the Maker** The Maker knows how to keep things running. Heavenly Father is kind, and we copy Him.

And charity suffereth long, and is kind, and envieth not, and is not puffed up, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil, and rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in the truth, beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
As Heavenly Father is kind, we also should be kind to others.
Copy the Maker.

story.title: David shows kindness to Mephibosheth

blocks.text: David was king. Jonathan's son had every reason to be afraid of him. David chose kindness.

And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
David began with, “Fear not.” He took away the fear first. Then he gave a place at his table. Kindness often starts by making someone feel safe.

And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is how a Christlike person treats others.
Welcome as He does.

Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is a passport that opens doors and fashions friends.
Kindness is the key.
**A door for every neighbor** We don't leave the door open for just a few. Everyone is welcome.
Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves? And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.
Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Remember This: Kindness Begins with Me” from the April 2011 general conference.
Jesus taught us through this story that everyone is our neighbor.
Open it to all.

A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kind words not only lift our spirits in the moment they are given, but they can linger with us over the years.
They remember the welcome.
**Our Father's home** Heavenly Father keeps His door open to us. We learn to keep ours open to others.

And charity suffereth long, and is kind, and envieth not, and is not puffed up, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil, and rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in the truth, beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.

Keep the door open.

story.title: Jacob and Esau meet

blocks.text: Jacob feared his brother Esau. They had been apart for years, and the last time had been bitter.
And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.
Esau opened his arms first. He ran to meet his brother. Years of distance ended with one kind act.

opening.text: Drop a pebble into still water. A ring forms. Then another, wider one. The ripples keep going long after the pebble has sunk. A small act of kindness is a pebble. We toss it, and we may never see where the last ripple lands.

mainMessage.text: Kindness is a pebble in a pond. Its ripples travel farther than we can see.

blocks.text: **The pond is heaven's** The water and the ripples are part of God's own life. Kindness begins there.
Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering;
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is the essence of a celestial life.
It begins in heaven.

And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is how a Christlike person treats others.
Follow His splash.
**Rings that make friends** Each ring reaches someone new. Kindness widens our circle of friends.
Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is a passport that opens doors and fashions friends.
The circle grows.
**Reaching every shore** Ripples don't pick a bank. Kindness shouldn't either. Everyone is our neighbor.
Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves? And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.
Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Remember This: Kindness Begins with Me” from the April 2011 general conference.
Jesus taught us through this story that everyone is our neighbor.
Reach every shore.
**Ripples that linger** Long after the splash, the water still moves. Kind words stay with a person for years.
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kind words not only lift our spirits in the moment they are given, but they can linger with us over the years.
The ripples last.
**Thrown by our Father's example** Heavenly Father is kind to everyone. We learn to throw from Him.

And charity suffereth long, and is kind, and envieth not, and is not puffed up, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil, and rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in the truth, beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

Throw as He throws.

story.title: Joseph forgives his brothers

blocks.text: Joseph's brothers had sold him. Years later, they stood before him afraid.
Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.
Joseph didn't repay them in kind. He comforted them. His kindness reached his brothers, his father and a whole family that would otherwise have starved.

opening.text: On a hot day, a cup of cool water is worth more than almost anything. It costs nearly nothing. It takes a minute to pour. But the person who drinks it remembers. Kindness is a cup of cool water. It is small, and it is sometimes exactly what a person needs.

mainMessage.text: Kindness is a cup of cool water handed to someone who is thirsty for a gentle word.

blocks.text: **Water from a heavenly spring** Kindness comes from God. It is part of the life He lives.
Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering;

Kindness is the essence of a celestial life.
The spring is heaven.

Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kindness is how a Christlike person treats others.
Pour as He pours.
**A cup that makes friends** Share a cup, and you share a moment. Friendships start there.
Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

Kindness is a passport that opens doors and fashions friends.
Share the cup.

Jesus taught us through this story that everyone is our neighbor.

A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Virtue of Kindness” from the April 2005 general conference.
Kind words not only lift our spirits in the moment they are given, but they can linger with us over the years.
The memory stays.
**Our Father gives first** Heavenly Father pours kindness on all of us. We pass the cup along.

And charity suffereth long, and is kind, and envieth not, and is not puffed up, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil, and rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in the truth, beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

story.title: David spares Saul

blocks.text: Saul had hunted David. Then David had Saul in his power, and let him go.
And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.
David could have taken revenge. He chose mercy. Even Saul saw the difference. Kindness shown to an enemy can change a heart.
